inspection.policy: Every hard gate is scored pass or fail from this image alone; partial or ambiguous evidence is fail.

frozen_gate_results.image_grounded_evidence: The frame visibly combines cream machinery and a worn turquoise cart, black molded analog knobs, chrome-rimmed hardware and a ribbed metal robot, multiple radiation/load gauges, and orbiting-electron emblems on the machine, sleeve, and wall.

A glass-roof greenhouse, cobalt fruit vines, and reactor instrumentation are visible, but condensation-beaded growing tubes or a clearly readable glass-tube hydroponic system are not present; ordinary orchard branches dominate that part of the frame.

The adult worker's right fingers visibly turn a control on the labeled seed-vault while her other hand rests at its diagnostic drawer; the analog robot simultaneously holds one glowing cobalt fruit in articulated tongs.
The woman wears a practical silver lamé coverall and a clear-front dosimeter; a transparent bubble helmet is visibly stored on the service cart at lower right.

Atomic-age cues occupy the arched greenhouse architecture, the large analog seed-vault and robot machinery, and the subject's silver work gear, dosimeter, and bubble helmet rather than appearing as one isolated emblem.
Physical analog meters, knobs, cables, enamel equipment, greenhouse structure, and atomic service signage dominate; neon megacity, holographic, and circuit-armor cyberpunk cues do not dominate.
The technology reads as enamel-and-chrome atomic science with molded controls and radiation meters, not Victorian boilers, exposed clockwork, steam machinery, soot, or interwar war engines.
Exactly one primary adult woman is visible; her face, two arms, two hands, and all visible fingers are coherent at the control and drawer contact points, without duplicated or fused anatomy.

Her unobscured face visibly carries long dark wavy hair, a gently oval face, brown eyes, natural straight-to-softly-arched brows, and softly defined coral lips. This is a visible-trait comparison only; biometric identity is not evaluated.
The result reads as one coherent photograph with plausible glasshouse depth, metal wear, cable weight, fabric folds, chrome reflections, warm/cobalt light interaction, and contact shadows.

candidate_gate_results.image_grounded_evidence: A curved greenhouse roof and an ATOMIC SERVICE / CIVILIAN ROCKET SUPPORT sign are visible, but an actual civilian rocket-service gantry with clearly integrated operating meters is not visually present; the candidate survives mainly as signage.

Thick corrugated cables and analog gauges exist, but no uninterrupted shielded umbilical visibly links the seed-vault to a distinct finned floor socket, and a connector bank plus two load gauges plus a clear dosimetry window are not separately legible as one mechanism.

The lower seed-vault drawer is visibly open with a glowing cobalt sample under a small probe/detector and two adjacent needle gauges directly beneath it, reading as a shielded dose/load diagnostic assembly.

A worn turquoise cart beside the robot visibly holds a coiled replacement sensor/cable and scuffed circular shield collar on top, while a lower return tray contains a separate spent umbilical with a physical warning tag.

repair_assessment.reason: The failures are visibility and separation failures that can be addressed by one wider, lower, open-dimension framing/composition/camera repair without changing the locked subject, event, concept, or appearance-reference use.
